coverage_gaps: The visible Layer 1B evidence is concentrated in U.S.-listed data-center power delivery, electrical equipment, and mission-critical construction; the merged universe may underrepresent non-U.S. grid equipment leaders, transformer manufacturers, cable suppliers, and EPC firms.

Need current company-level backlog, book-to-bill, lead-time, and capacity-expansion disclosures for electrical equipment vendors, transformer manufacturers, grid EPC contractors, and switchgear suppliers before upgrading or downgrading rankings.
Need region-by-region U.S. load-growth and interconnection map across PJM, ERCOT, MISO, SERC, WECC, CAISO, and NYISO to distinguish local utility beneficiaries from generic power-sector exposure.
Need utility IRP, rate-case, and large-load tariff evidence to determine whether grid capex economics accrue to regulated utilities, suppliers, IPPs, data-center customers, or ratepayers.
Need gas-turbine backlog, delivery-slot availability, pipeline constraint, and power-market evidence before ranking natural-gas equipment, midstream, and commodity gas names.
Need nuclear fuel-cycle contract evidence across uranium, conversion, enrichment, and HALEU; spot uranium narratives alone are insufficient for Serenity validation.
Need renewables/storage validation focused on interconnection-ready assets, grid-forming controls, storage backlog, curtailment economics, and tax-credit policy risk rather than broad solar beta.

Need market-pricing check in later layers: valuation, revenue exposure, margin expansion, order conversion, short interest/crowding, and whether obvious beneficiaries have already priced in the chokepoint.

evidence.claim: IEA states that global electricity demand is expected to grow rapidly in 2025 and 2026, supported by industry, appliances, air conditioning, data centres, EVs, and other electrification drivers.
evidence.source_title: Global electricity demand to keep growing robustly through 2026 despite economic headwinds

evidence.claim: IEA Electricity 2026 frames the period as an 'Age of Electricity' with growing consumption from AI, data centres, electrification of industry, transport, and buildings, and includes focused analysis on grids and flexibility.
IEA Electricity 2026 says renewables, natural gas, and nuclear together are expected to meet all additional global electricity demand in aggregate over 2026-2030.

NERC's 2025 Long-Term Reliability Assessment highlights intensifying resource-adequacy risks over the next decade and notes that data-center projects have moved from speculative/exploratory stages into development commitments that affect load forecasting.
DOE's Office of Electricity states that distribution transformers are building blocks of the electric grid and are facing supply-chain constraints, long lead times, and component shortages.

DOE reports that COVID-era supply and labor constraints plus material shortages drove distribution-transformer lead times from three to six months in 2019 to 12 to 30 months in 2023, the latest available data cited on the DOE page.

FERC directed PJM to establish transparent rules to facilitate service for AI-driven data centers and other large loads co-located with generating facilities, while addressing reliability and capacity-addition concerns.
evidence.source_title: FERC Directs Nation’s Largest Grid Operator to Create New Rules to Embrace Innovation and Protect Consumers

evidence.claim: IEA's Gas Market Report Q1 2026 states that global LNG supply growth is set to accelerate in 2026, supporting stronger natural-gas demand and a new all-time high.

EIA's AEO2026 analysis projects U.S. dry natural gas production to increase significantly over coming decades, meeting growing domestic and international demand, and includes a case exploring higher power demand from data centers.
evidence.source_title: Domestic and international demand drive natural gas production growth

evidence.claim: DOE announced that Centrus produced about 900 kilograms of HALEU by June 2025, describing HALEU as a crucial fuel source needed by most advanced reactor designs.
evidence.source_title: Centrus Reaches 900 Kilogram Mark for HALEU Production

evidence.claim: World Nuclear Association states that HALEU will be needed for many advanced power reactor fuels and more than half of SMR designs in development.
IEA's Global Critical Minerals Outlook 2025 notes that expanding construction and electrification of grids and industrial equipment are fueling increased copper demand.
evidence.source_title: Overview of outlook for key minerals - Global Critical Minerals Outlook 2025

evidence.claim: Digital Realty's March 2026 investor presentation says AI affects customer engagement, data-center design, and product offerings, and says PlatformDIGITAL is positioned to benefit from AI training and inference.

Equinix disclosed 52 active major development projects as of January 2026 across 35 metros, expected to deliver more than 55,000 cabinets of retail capacity and more than 100 MW of xScale capacity through 2028.
Dominion's annual-report filing says much of its growth is being driven by the data-center industry and that it has been connecting an average of 15 data centers per year.
evidence.source_title: Dominion Energy 2025 Annual Report and Proxy Filing

evidence.claim: Data Center Dynamics reported that Dominion described more than 48 GW of data-center-related pipeline in various stages of contracting as of December 2025 and a higher five-year capital plan tied largely to Virginia demand.
evidence.source_title: Dominion reports marginal increase in data center pipeline

evidence.claim: Vistra describes itself as a leading integrated retail electricity and power-generation company; its 2026 CERAWeek materials discuss rapidly growing energy demand, data-center demand, reliability, and nuclear power's role.
evidence.source_title: CERAWeek 2026: Powering What’s Next - Vistra Corp.

evidence.claim: IES states that it designs and installs integrated electrical and technology systems and provides infrastructure products and services to end markets including data centers.
IES fiscal 2026 first-quarter materials state that results reflected continued solid demand and execution in the data-center end market.
evidence.source_title: IES Holdings Reports Fiscal 2026 First Quarter Results

memory_update.text: Energy Layer 1 should be treated primarily as electricity-system expansion rather than a generic commodity-energy basket.
Highest-quality first-pass chokepoints are grid transformers, medium-voltage switchgear, substations, transmission/distribution EPC, and mission-critical electrical construction.

Data centers belong in the universe as demand-node validators, but their Serenity score should be below scarce equipment and construction bottlenecks unless powered-capacity pricing evidence is strong.
Nuclear workstream should prioritize fuel-cycle scarcity, HALEU, enrichment, conversion, and long-term contracting before speculative SMR deployment stories.
Gas and LNG names need decomposition into commodity gas, midstream constraints, LNG export capacity, gas turbines, on-site generation, and dispatchable power economics.
Layer 2 must add company-specific evidence for non-visible candidates, especially Eaton, Quanta, GE Vernova, Constellation, BWXT, Cameco, Cheniere, midstream gas names, storage, and renewables.
Deduplication retained one active CEG candidate; future pipeline should enforce ticker uniqueness before scoring to avoid duplicate rows.

summary: Merged Layer 1A theme map and visible Layer 1B node candidates into an initial Serenity universe for Energy reframed as electricity-system expansion. Highest-priority names cluster around grid bottlenecks, electrical equipment, data-center power delivery, mission-critical electrical construction, regulated utility load growth, firm power, nuclear fuel-cycle scarcity, gas/LNG infrastructure, renewables/storage integration, and critical materials. Ranking is Serenity relevance only, before valuation, crowding, and full company-level evidence validation.
universe_method: multi-step: theme decomposition -> node expansion -> dedupe/rank
